description: Wire protocol between the aseprite-agent bridge and the Aseprite extension (JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket). This file is the single definition: the extension ships it, the bridge copies it, and contract tests check both sides against it. Bump version on any incompatible change.

handshake.hello: extension -> bridge, first message: { token, protocol, asepriteVersion }
handshake.welcome: bridge -> extension: the connection is accepted
handshake.incompatible: bridge -> extension, then close: { expected, received, message }

kinds.read: Leaves the document alone. Runs as is, also for a sub-agent.
kinds.write: Changes the document in a way the scope guard can't check (undo history, palette, slices, another sprite). Captured as an edit step; refused for a sub-agent's scope.
kinds.scoped-write: Changes cels, layers or frames of the active sprite. Captured as an edit step; for a sub-agent's scope, undone when it changed anything outside the scope.
kinds.needsSprite: Whether the request needs an active sprite ("No active sprite" otherwise). Default: true for writes, false for reads.

params.types: Each request lists its params as name: type. Types: string, integer, number, boolean, array, object, any, layer, frame, frames. A trailing ? marks it optional. Unknown params are an error, except scope (sub-agent scopes), which any request may carry.
params.layer: A layer id ('L12', or 12) or a layer name (searched through groups, top first). The extension resolves it to the layer's id before the handler runs; a missing layer is an error.
params.frame: A 1-based frame number in range. Omitted means the active frame; the extension fills it in.
params.frames: A frame spec: a number, a list of numbers, 'a-b' (inclusive), or 'all'. The extension resolves it to a list of frame numbers in range; out-of-range frames are an error. 'frames?all' defaults to every frame, 'frames?active' to the active frame, plain 'frames?' leaves it out.

blendModes: put_image and put_images take blend_mode for the layer they make (new_layer): normal, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, color_dodge, color_burn, hard_light, soft_light, difference, exclusion, hue, saturation, color, luminosity, addition, subtract or divide; get_state reports each image layer's blendMode by the same names. opacity is 0-255.
putImages: put_images writes several images in one undo step: images is a list of put_image params (width, height, rgba, frame (required), new_layer or layer, above (a layer id or name, also one made earlier in the same request), x, y, hide, blend_mode, opacity, and locked (#79: true locks the new_layer, layer.isEditable = false, after every image is written; the layer that was active stays active)). frames: the sprite gets at least this many frames first; each new frame copies the cels of the last frame (as Aseprite's New Frame does) and lasts duration ms (default: the last frame's). palette: hex colors appended to the sprite palette before the images are written (the ones it lacks, compared as normalized hex), in the same undo step; the result counts them as paletteAdded. insert (#70): [{ after, durations: [ms], shift?: { layers, offsets: [{ x, y }] } }] puts len(durations) frames right after frame `after` (numbered as before any insert), before frames are added at the end; on every image layer the new frames' cels are linked to the cel in `after`, except shift.layers, which get copies moved by each offset. Tags covering `after` grow, later tags and recorded hits move. durations: [{ frame, ms }] then sets frame durations, and hit: { frame, freeze_ms, shake_ms?, amp? } is appended to the sprite property aseprite-agent "fx.hits" (get_state's activeSprite.fxHits). Image frames, durations and hit use the numbering after the inserts; the result counts inserted frames. With insert, durations or hit, images may be empty. get_state lists each layer's linked cels as celLinks (groups of frames sharing one image). fx (#71): { layer, id, x, y, fps, loop, windup_ms } records an effect for export in the layer property aseprite-agent "fx" (after the images, in the same undo step; layer is an id or name, also 'AI: <new_layer>' made in this request); create_animation takes the same fx without layer for its one layer. get_state reports it on the layer as fx: { id, x, y, fps, loop, windupMs } (x, y: the effect's origin in sprite pixels; windupMs: ms from its start to its impact). fx may also carry recipe (#72: an FX recipe's JSON) and render (JSON of the render settings that differ from the effect's defaults), text of at most 16384 characters each, reported back on the layer's fx as given. With fx, images may be empty. spec (#79): a pixel spec's JSON, text of at most 65536 characters, stored in the sprite property aseprite-agent "concept.spec" in the same undo step (an empty text removes it); get_state reports it as activeSprite.pixelSpec. With spec, images may be empty. get_state reports each layer's lock as editable.
binaryResults: A request marked binary answers with a result containing binary: true, followed by exactly one binary WebSocket frame with the data.
bridgeMethodIds: Requests the extension sends use string ids, so they never collide with the bridge's numeric ids.
